subject: maths
title: Telling the Time
seo_title: Year 3 Telling the Time Worksheets: Clocks to the Minute, am and pm (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Tell and write the time from an analogue clock, including using Roman numerals from I to XII, and 12-hour and 24-hour clocks; estimate and read time with increasing accuracy to the nearest minute; record and compare time in terms of seconds, minutes and hours; use vocabulary such as o’clock, a.m./p.m., morning, afternoon, noon and midnight; know the number of seconds in a minute and the number of days in each month, year and leap year; compare durations of events.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 maths worksheets on telling the time: o’clock, half past, quarter past and quarter to, times to 5 minutes and to the minute, Roman numeral clocks, am and pm, days in each month, leap years and how long events last. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Short hand: the hour. Long hand: count in 5s for the minutes.
key_sub: Right-hand side: minutes past. Left-hand side: minutes to the next hour, so 25 to 9 is 8:35. am is before noon, pm is after noon.
body_html:
The two hands

The short hand shows the hour. The long hand shows the minutes. Each number on the clock is 5 minutes for the long hand, so count in 5s.

Past and to

When the long hand is on the right-hand side, say minutes past the hour. When it is on the left-hand side, say minutes to the next hour.

DigitalWe say
4:004 o’clock
4:15quarter past 4
4:2020 past 4
4:30half past 4
4:3525 to 5
4:45quarter to 5
4:5010 to 5

To the nearest minute

Between two numbers there are 5 small marks, one for each minute. Count in 5s to the last number, then on in 1s.

Read to the minute

The long hand is 3 small marks past the 4. The short hand is between 6 and 7.

Count in 5s to the 4: 5, 10, 15, 20. Then 21, 22, 23.

Answer: 23 minutes past 6 (6:23)

Roman numeral clocks

Some clocks use Roman numerals. Read them in the same way.

IIIIIIIVVVIVIIVIIIIXXXIXII
123456789101112

am, pm, noon and midnight

am is from midnight to noon (night and morning). pm is from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening). Noon is 12 o’clock in the day. Midnight is 12 o’clock at night.

am or pm?

Isla eats breakfast at 25 to 8. Write the time.

25 to 8 is 35 minutes past 7. Breakfast is in the morning, so it is am.

Answer: 7:35 am

Time facts

UnitEquals
1 minute60 seconds
1 hour60 minutes
1 day24 hours
1 week7 days
1 year12 months, 365 days
1 leap year366 days (29 February)

“30 days has September, April, June and November. All the rest have 31, except February.” February has 28 days, or 29 in a leap year.

How long? Count on

An hour has 60 minutes, not 100. Jump to the next o’clock first, then on to the end time.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
“25 to 9” written as 9:3525 to 9 is before 9 o’clock: 60 − 25 = 35, so 8:35
Long hand on 4 read as 4 minutesEach number is 5 minutes: 4 × 5 = 20 minutes
Half past 3 read as half past 4The short hand has not reached 4 yet, so the hour is still 3
Breakfast at 7:30 pmMorning times are am: 7:30 am
February has 30 daysFebruary has 28 days, or 29 in a leap year
3:45 to 4:20 worked out as 420 − 345 = 75 minutesCount on: 15 + 20 = 35 minutes

faq.q: What time should a Year 3 child be able to tell?
faq.a: By the end of Year 3, children should tell the time to the nearest minute on an analogue clock, including clocks with Roman numerals, and write it as a 12-hour time with am or pm.

faq.q: What is the difference between am and pm?
faq.a: am times are from midnight to noon (night and morning). pm times are from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening). So breakfast is usually am and tea is pm.

faq.q: How many days are in each month?
faq.a: April, June, September and November have 30 days. February has 28 days, or 29 in a leap year. All the other months have 31 days.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn to tell the time?
faq.a: Use a real analogue clock at home and ask the time at everyday moments, such as breakfast or bedtime. Start with o’clock and half past, then quarter past and quarter to, then count in 5s for the other times.

The short hour hand is between 9 and 10, so the hour is still 9. The long minute hand points to 4. Count in 5s: 4 × 5 = 20 minutes past. The minute hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past 9. It is 20 past 9.

items.q: The digital clock shows a time. How do we say it?
items.e: 8:35 is 35 minutes past 8. That is more than half past, so say to the next hour. 60 − 35 = 25 minutes to 9: 25 to 9.

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. The long minute hand points to 10. Count in 5s: 10 × 5 = 50 minutes past. That is 10 minutes before 8 o’clock (60 − 50 = 10). The minute hand is on the left-hand side, so we say to 8. It is 10 to 8.

The short hour hand is between 5 and 6, so the hour is still 5. The long minute hand points to 1. Count in 5s: 1 × 5 = 5 minutes past. The minute hand is on the right-hand side, so we say past 5. It is 5 past 5.

items.q: The digital clock shows a time. How do we say it?
items.e: 4:20 is 20 minutes after 4 o’clock. It is less than half past, so say past: 20 past 4.

The short hour hand is between X (10) and XI (11), so the hour is still 10. The long minute hand points to VII (7). Count in 5s: 7 × 5 = 35 minutes past. That is 25 minutes before 11 o’clock (60 − 35 = 25). The minute hand is on the left-hand side, so we say to 11. It is 25 to 11.

items.q: The digital clock shows a time. How do we say it?
items.e: 2:50 is 50 minutes past 2. That is more than half past, so say to the next hour. 60 − 50 = 10 minutes to 3: 10 to 3.

items.q: The digital clock shows a time. How do we say it?
items.e: 11:40 is 40 minutes past 11. That is more than half past, so say to the next hour. 60 − 40 = 20 minutes to 12: 20 to 12.

sets.title: To the minute: am, pm, noon and midnight

c: 12 o’clock in the middle of the day
items.e: Noon is 12 o’clock in the middle of the day. Midnight is 12 o’clock at night.

c: 12 o’clock in the middle of the day
items.e: Midnight is 12 o’clock at night, when one day ends and the next day starts.
am times go from midnight to noon (night and morning). pm times go from noon to midnight (afternoon and evening).
The afternoon is after noon, so it is a pm time. 2:30 am is in the middle of the night. So the answer is 2:30 pm.

items.q: Which is a sensible time for school to start?
items.e: School starts in the morning, so it is an am time. 3:50 am is the middle of the night. So the answer is 8:50 am.
Midnight is 12 o’clock at night. 11:50 pm is 10 minutes before midnight. 11:50 am is 10 minutes before noon. So the answer is 11:50 pm.

items.q: It is 11:30 am. What time will it be 1 hour later?
items.e: 1 hour after 11:30 is 12:30. It is now after noon, so it changes to pm: 12:30 pm. (12:30 am is just after midnight.)

The short hour hand is between 12 and 1, so the hour is still 12. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 3. Count in 5s to 15, then on in 1s: 18 minutes past. It is after noon, so it is pm. So it is 12:18 pm.

The short hour hand is between 3 and 4, so the hour is still 3. The long minute hand is 2 small marks past the 4. Count in 5s to 20, then on in 1s: 22 minutes past. It is after noon, so it is pm. So it is 3:22 pm.

The short hour hand is between 5 and 6, so the hour is still 5. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 8. Count in 5s to 40, then on in 1s: 43 minutes past. It is after noon, so it is pm. So it is 5:43 pm.

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. The long minute hand is 4 small marks past the 4. Count in 5s to 20, then on in 1s: 24 minutes past. It is after noon, so it is pm. So it is 7:24 pm.

The short hour hand is between 7 and 8, so the hour is still 7. The long minute hand is 1 small mark past the 4. Count in 5s to 20, then on in 1s: 21 minutes past. It is the morning, so it is am. So it is 7:21 am.

The short hour hand is between 8 and 9, so the hour is still 8. The long minute hand is 3 small marks past the 6. Count in 5s to 30, then on in 1s: 33 minutes past. It is the morning, so it is am. So it is 8:33 am.

items.q: Write 20 past 10 in the morning as a digital time.
items.e: “20 past 10” means 20 minutes after 10 o’clock: 10:20. It is in the morning, so it is am: 10:20 am.

items.q: Write 25 to 9 in the morning as a digital time.
items.e: “25 to 9” means 25 minutes before 9 o’clock. 60 − 25 = 35, so it is 35 minutes past 8: 8:35. It is in the morning, so it is am: 8:35 am. (Not 9:35 am: that is after 9 o’clock.)

items.q: Write 20 to 5 in the afternoon as a digital time.
items.e: “20 to 5” means 20 minutes before 5 o’clock. 60 − 20 = 40, so it is 40 minutes past 4: 4:40. It is in the afternoon, so it is pm: 4:40 pm. (Not 5:40 pm: that is after 5 o’clock.)

items.q: Write 5 to 8 in the evening as a digital time.
items.e: “5 to 8” means 5 minutes before 8 o’clock. 60 − 5 = 55, so it is 55 minutes past 7: 7:55. It is in the evening, so it is pm: 7:55 pm. (Not 8:55 pm: that is after 8 o’clock.)

items.q: On a 24-hour clock, what is 3 pm?
items.e: pm times are after noon. Add 12 to the hour: 3 + 12 = 15. So 3 pm is 15:00.

items.q: A 24-hour clock shows 18:30. What is this in 12-hour time?
items.e: Take away 12 from the hour: 18 − 12 = 6. It is in the evening, so it is 6:30 pm. (Do not just drop the 1: 18:30 is not 8:30.)

items.q: How is midnight shown on a 24-hour clock?
items.e: On a 24-hour clock a new day starts at midnight, so midnight is 00:00. 12:00 is noon.

sets.title: Time facts: seconds, minutes, days and months

items.e: There are 60 seconds in 1 minute.
There are 60 minutes in 1 hour. (Not 100: time does not count in hundreds.)
There are 24 hours in 1 day: 12 am hours and 12 pm hours. 12 + 12 = 24.
Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday: 7 days. (5 is just the school days.)
January to December: 12 months. (52 is the number of weeks.)

items.q: How many days are in a year that is not a leap year?
items.e: A normal year has 365 days. A leap year has 1 more: 366.

items.q: How many days are in a leap year?
items.e: A leap year has 1 extra day, 29 February. 365 + 1 = 366 days.

items.q: How many days does February have in a normal year?
items.e: February is the shortest month. It has 28 days, and 29 days in a leap year. It never has 30.

items.q: In a leap year, how many days does February have?
items.e: In a leap year February gets 1 extra day: 28 + 1 = 29 days.
Remember: “30 days has September, April, June and November. All the rest have 31, except February.” So September has 30 days.
Remember: “30 days has September, April, June and November. All the rest have 31, except February.” So July has 31 days.
Remember: “30 days has September, April, June and November. All the rest have 31, except February.” So April has 30 days.
Remember: “30 days has September, April, June and November. All the rest have 31, except February.” June, September and November have 30 days. August has 31.

items.q: How many minutes are in half an hour?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. Half of 60 is 30 minutes. (Not 50: an hour is not 100 minutes.)

items.q: How many minutes are in a quarter of an hour?
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. A quarter of 60 is 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes. (25 would be a quarter of 100.)
1 minute = 60 seconds. 60 + 30 = 90 seconds. (Not 130: a minute is 60 seconds, not 100.)
Change them all to seconds. 2 minutes = 60 + 60 = 120 seconds. 120 is more than 100 and 90. So 2 minutes is the longest.
1 minute = 60 seconds. 50 seconds is less than 60 seconds, 70 seconds and 1 hour. So 50 seconds is the shortest.

items.q: About how long does it take to brush your teeth?
items.e: 2 seconds is far too quick, and 2 hours is far too long. Brushing your teeth takes about 2 minutes.

items.q: About how long does a Year 3 child sleep at night?
items.e: Children sleep from the evening until the morning. That is about 10 hours.

items.q: A TV programme starts at 4:10 pm and ends at 4:35 pm. How long is it?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 35 − 10 = 25 minutes.

items.q: Lily starts reading at 7:05 pm and stops at 7:45 pm. How long does she read for?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 45 − 5 = 40 minutes.

items.q: Morning break starts at 10:30 am and ends at 10:45 am. How long is break?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 45 − 30 = 15 minutes.

items.q: Arjun’s piano lesson is from 5:20 pm to 5:50 pm. How long is the lesson?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 50 − 20 = 30 minutes.

items.q: Assembly starts at 9:05 am and ends at 9:27 am. How long is assembly?
items.e: Both times are in the same hour. 27 − 5 = 22 minutes.

items.q: A football match starts at 2:45 pm and ends at 3:30 pm. How long is the match?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 2:45 pm to 3:00 pm is 15 minutes. Then 3:00 pm to 3:30 pm is 30 minutes. 15 + 30 = 45 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: Amelia gets on the school bus at 8:40 am. She gets to school at 9:05 am. How long is the bus ride?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 8:40 am to 9:00 am is 20 minutes. Then 9:00 am to 9:05 am is 5 minutes. 20 + 5 = 25 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: Noah’s swimming lesson is from 3:50 pm to 4:35 pm. How long is it?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 3:50 pm to 4:00 pm is 10 minutes. Then 4:00 pm to 4:35 pm is 35 minutes. 10 + 35 = 45 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: A cake goes in the oven at 11:48 am. It comes out at 12:13 pm. How long does it bake?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 11:48 am to 12:00 pm is 12 minutes. Then 12:00 pm to 12:13 pm is 13 minutes. 12 + 13 = 25 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: A film starts at 5:50 pm and ends at 7:20 pm. How long is the film?
items.e: Count on to the next o’clock first: 5:50 pm to 6:00 pm is 10 minutes. Then 6:00 pm to 7:20 pm is 1 hour 20 minutes. 10 + 80 = 90 minutes = 1 hour 30 minutes. (An hour has 60 minutes, not 100, so do not just take away the numbers.)

items.q: A TV programme starts at 6:15 pm. It lasts 25 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Count on 25 minutes from 6:15: 15 + 25 = 40. It is still the evening, so it ends at 6:40 pm.

items.q: Lunchtime starts at 12:10 pm. It lasts 50 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: 12:10 + 50 minutes: 10 + 50 = 60 minutes, which is a new hour. So it ends at 1:00 pm.

items.q: Evie goes to bed at 7:30 pm. She has a bath 20 minutes before bed. What time does the bath start?
items.e: Count back 20 minutes from 7:30: 30 − 20 = 10. The bath starts at 7:10 pm. (7:50 pm is 20 minutes after bedtime.)

items.q: A film starts at 5:40 pm. It lasts 1 hour 35 minutes. What time does it end?
items.e: Add 1 hour: 5:40 pm → 6:40 pm. Then add 35 minutes: 20 minutes takes you to 7:00 pm, and 15 more makes 7:15 pm.

items.q: School starts at 8:50 am and ends at 3:20 pm. How long is the school day?
items.e: 8:50 am to 2:50 pm is 6 hours. 2:50 pm to 3:20 pm is 30 minutes. So the school day is 6 hours 30 minutes.

items.q: Charlie’s film lasts 1 hour 30 minutes. Ava’s film lasts 95 minutes. Whose film is longer, and by how much?
items.e: 1 hour 30 minutes = 60 + 30 = 90 minutes. 95 − 90 = 5. So Ava’s film is longer, by 5 minutes.

items.q: Mohammed runs a race in 58 seconds. Freya takes 1 minute 5 seconds. How much faster is Mohammed?
items.e: 1 minute 5 seconds = 60 + 5 = 65 seconds. 65 − 58 = 7 seconds. (Not 47: a minute is 60 seconds, not 100.)

items.q: Harry practises the recorder for 15 minutes a day for 4 days. How long is that in total?
items.e: 4 × 15 = 60 minutes. 60 minutes = 1 hour.

items.q: Today is 27 April. The school trip is in 5 days. What is the date of the trip?
items.e: April has 30 days. Count on: 28, 29, 30 April, then 1 May, 2 May. The trip is on 2 May.

items.q: How many days are there in June and July together?
items.e: June has 30 days and July has 31 days. 30 + 31 = 61 days.
